chunks: Muhammad b. Ali Majiluwayh (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Muhammad b. Yahya al-Attar narrated to us. He said: Sahl b. Ziyad al-Adami narrated to us. He said: Uthman b. Isa narrated to me from Khalid b. Najih from Abi Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him). He said:

Misery was discussed in his presence, so he said: Misery is in three things: in a woman, in a creature, and in a house. As for the misery of a woman, it is in the exorbitance of her dowry and the disobedience of her husband. As for the creature, it is in its poor behaviour and its prevention of riding its back. As for the house, it is in the narrowness of its yard, the evil of its neighbours, and the plenitude of its faults.
ai.seo_question: What are the three types of misery according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (as) identifies three sources of misery in daily life: in a woman (excessive dowry and disobedience to her husband), in an animal (poor temperament and refusal to be ridden), and in a house (narrow yard, bad neighbours, many defects). This teaching was practical advice for the 4th-century Hijri audience, addressing the most common sources of daily hardship and guiding believers toward wise decisions in marriage, commerce, and dwelling.
